title: Trilce: Poem XXIX — Bottled Boredom Buzzes
text:
Bottled boredom buzzes

beneath the unproduced moment and cane.


A parallel passes beside

an ungrateful broken line of happiness.

Each firmness startles me, beside that water

moving away, laughing steel, falling silent.


Retempered thread, thread, binomial thread—

where will you break, knot of war?


Armor this equator, Moon.
editorial_note: Vallejo's mathematical and material collisions are kept syntactically abrasive; improducido remains the coined unproduced.

title: Trilce: Poem XIV — As for My Explanation
text:
As for my explanation.

This lacerates me with earlyness.

That way of walking along trapezes.

Those courageous brutes, like false additions.

That gum gluing quicksilver to the inside.

Those buttocks seated upward.

That cannot be, been.

Absurd.

Dementia.

But I have come from Trujillo to Lima.

But I earn a salary of five soles.
editorial_note: Tempranía becomes earlyness and the impossible tense of sido remains exposed; the final salary keeps its blunt socioeconomic descent.

title: Trilce: Poem XXIV — At the Edge of a Flowering Tomb
text:
At the edge of a flowering tomb

two Marys pass by weeping,

weeping seas.


The plucked rhea of memory

stretches out its final feather,

and with it Peter's negative hand

engraves upon a Palm Sunday

resonances of obsequies and stones.


From the edge of a disturbed tomb

two Marys walk away singing.


Monday.
editorial_note: The biblical sequence and Vallejo's Andean rhea remain together; Monday lands as the desacralizing final stone.

title: Trilce: Poem XII — I Escape a Feint, Filament by Filament
text:
I escape a feint, filament by filament.

A projectile—I do not know where it will fall.

Uncertainty. Sundown. Cervical joint.


Snap of a blowfly dying

halfway through its flight and falling to earth.

What does Newton say now?

But naturally, you are children.


Uncertainty. Heels that do not turn.

Little face knotted, forge-wrought,

five thorns along one side

and five along the other: Hush! It is coming out.
editorial_note: Scientific causality, anatomy, and birth-like emergence remain deliberately disjointed; fabrida is rendered as forge-wrought.

title: Trilce: Poem VIII — Tomorrow Is That-Other Day
text:
Tomorrow is that-other day; perhaps

I would find, for the hyphaltic power,

an eternal entrance.


Tomorrow, some day,

the plated shop would be

with a pair of pericardia, a couple

of carnivores in heat.


All that may well take root.

But a tomorrow without tomorrow,

between the rings we are widowed of,

there will be a margin of mirror

through which I shall pass my own forehead

until I lose the echo

and remain with my brow toward my back.
editorial_note: The invented hifalto is carried as hyphaltic rather than normalized; bodily futurity folds into the impossible mirror.

title: I Dreamed an Escape. And I Dreamed…
text:
I dreamed an escape. And I dreamed

of your lace scattered through the room.

Along a pier, some mother;

and her fifteen years nursing an hour.


I dreamed an escape. A “forever”

breathed upon the stairway of a prow;

I dreamed a mother;

fresh little shoots of green,

and a bridal chest constellated with dawn.


Along a pier…

And along a throat that drowns!
editorial_note: Hora remains an hour rather than a child, preserving the surreal compression of youth, maternity, and time.

title: Trilce: Poem II — Time Time
text:
Time Time.

Noon stalled among damp chills.

The bored barracks pump bails out

time time time time.


Was Was.


Roosters song while scratching in vain.

Mouth of clear day conjugating

was was was was.


Tomorrow Tomorrow.


Rest still warm from being.

The present thinks keep me for

tomorrow tomorrow tomorrow tomorrow.


Name Name.


What is the name of all that bristles us?

Its name is Thesame that suffers

name name name namE.
editorial_note: Cantic verbal mutation and capitalization reproduce Vallejo's pressure on tense, naming, and sameness rather than smoothing grammar.

title: Sacred Defoliation
text:
Moon! Crown of an immense head,

shedding your leaves into golden shadows!

Red crown of a Jesus who thinks

tragically sweet thoughts of emeralds!


Moon! Crazed celestial heart,

why do you sail so, inside a goblet

filled with blue wine, toward the west,

like a defeated, suffering stern?


Moon! And by dint of flying in vain,

you immolate yourself in scattered opals:

perhaps you are my gypsy heart,

wandering the blue, weeping verses!…
editorial_note: The decadent jeweled imagery remains lush; deshojación binds lunar phases to petals, leaves, and sacrificial stripping.
